summary: Client 504 after prolonged stall on deep multi-document priming + high max_tokens
description: Issue summary: Customer experienced a client-facing 504 (gateway timeout) after a request with a ~45k token multi-document prompt and max_tokens=25000 stalled mid-generation. Impact: interactive analytics UI request failed, multiple users affected at the customer; request counted against billing. Environment: prod-us-east, dedicated tenant for PaperTrail Analytics (enterprise).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Upload 12 long documents (~10k tokens total priming) into the prompt. 2) Call completions API with model=redwood-llama-fulldoc-13b, max_tokens=25000, streaming=true. 3) Observe initial streaming chunks for ~15s, then stream stops sending data; client receives 504 from edge after ~90s.
observed_behavior: Initial tokens stream successfully. Around token ~11,800 the server stalls: no further chunks are emitted, connection stays open until upstream LB responds with 504. Logs show finalizer queue growing and repeated KV cache eviction messages. Customer saw 'Upstream read timeout'.
expected_behavior: Long-context requests should either stream continuously until completion or fail fast with a descriptive error if constraints (memory, kernel swap) are hit; should not silently stall until LB timeout.
logs_and_error_snippets:
[2026-03-10T13:22:11Z] INFO request_id=abc123 streaming chunk seq=1 size=2048
[2026-03-10T13:22:26Z] WARN request_id=abc123 kv_cache: evicting prefix entries (usage=93%)
[2026-03-10T13:22:40Z] ERROR request_id=abc123 finalizer: enqueue_latency=1200ms queue_depth=18
[2026-03-10T13:23:41Z] ERROR request_id=abc123 upstream: read timeout from load-balancer -> returned 504
Edge logs: nginx: 504 while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.2.3.45, server: api.redwood.internal
investigation_notes: Hypotheses considered: 1) KV cache eviction thrashing on very long priming leads to repeated recomputation and backpressure; 2) Kernel swap (GPU memory) observed for other similar incidents, causing the runtime to pause; 3) Finalizer queue backlog prevents last-chunk transmission. Checked metric dashboards: finalizer_queue_length spiked to 20 for the tenant, kernel_swap_count increased on host gpu-node-12, and per-request GPU utilization remained high (>95%). No recent deploys to serving-runtime around incident time. Similar behavior referenced in SUP-29541 but here we observe a distinct sequence number where streaming stops mid-response.
temporary_workarounds_proposed: 1) Advise customer to reduce max_tokens to <= 8k or split the job into shorter generation calls. 2) Temporarily disable aggressive KV caching for the tenant via tenant flag (ops toggle). 3) Route heavy long-context requests to a dedicated pool with higher memory headroom (if available) to avoid kernel swaps.

- Lena: kernel_swap_count correlates with stall windows; suspect memory fragmentation when priming with many docs.
